_comment: The Grade 3 Art & Design standalone lesson build, described for ../../mathematics/lesson-app-tools and built by ../lesson-kit. Order here IS the lesson number. Eight lessons against Cambridge Primary Art & Design 0067 Stage 3, pitched at the framework's Stages 3-4 progression text (the first stage with guidance of its own): a visual journal, graded pencils and charcoal for tone, the colour wheel and colour schemes, clay reliefs, one textile made three ways, murals for an audience, learning from named artists, and judging work against goals. Progress is written under u01..u08 beneath ehel-art-g03, whose catalogue entry is generated FROM this lesson list. objectiveFloors are recorded at the measured value after each build and may rise, not fall.
subject: art-and-design
_startingCheck: The readiness check before Lesson 1, over Grade 2's content: built by ../lesson-kit/build-check.py, linked from the hub, uploaded by deploy.mjs because it is in extraPages. Its review lessons are Grade 2's, linked in ../grade-2-v2/. It is not a lesson and reports nothing to the gradebook.
hubStrands: Gathering patterns from buildings in a sketchbook; trying pencils from hard to soft and charcoal; looking closely at a brick carved long ago, a stitched quilt, a painted house wall, a swirling night sky and a great wave; and comparing how different artists used their materials.
Showing light and shade with graded pencils; mixing across the colour wheel; building a clay relief; stitching, weaving or fusing a textile; and planning a mural with a mock-up before it is made big.
Checking our work against a goal; giving praise with one useful next step; saying how another artist's work helped us; and changing a colour scheme or a size to make work better.
Turning a sketch into a design; changing a mural after thinking about who will see it; borrowing a technique from an artist; and showing that one idea can be made in more than one way.
